episode.title: Adapt provider configuration and request routing for alternate OpenAI-compatible endpoints
episode.before: At parent ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7, the CLI exposed only an API key and API base. Coder.create required those values and directly assigned openai.api_key and openai.api_base. ChatCompletion requests contained model, messages, temperature, stream, and optional functions, but could not carry deployment_id or engine routing arguments required by some provider endpoints.
episode.after: At 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758, the CLI accepts optional provider base, type, version, deployment ID, and engine settings. Startup centrally assigns supplied settings to the provider SDK module while leaving unspecified optional settings untouched. Coder.create no longer owns credentials or endpoint configuration. Request construction conditionally forwards stored deployment_id and engine values to ChatCompletion.create.
episode.diff: The merge commit changes seven files with 95 insertions and 46 deletions relative to its first parent. The implementation adds four provider-related CLI arguments, moves API key/base ownership from the coder factory to application startup, generically maps five optional CLI values onto SDK module attributes, conditionally adds deployment_id and engine to request kwargs, updates all affected test call sites to the slimmer Coder.create interface, and documents alternate endpoint configuration. No dedicated behavioral test for the newly added provider fields was added.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758 is a merge of PR/issue 88 titled "Added args to configure openai module to access Azure" and has first parent ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json fields resolved_commit, parent_commit, linked_pull_requests; git show --format=fuller 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, Coder.create required openai_api_key, accepted openai_api_base with a fixed default, and assigned both values directly to the provider SDK module.
Before the change, main passed the parsed API key and API base positionally into Coder.create; the CLI offered no type, version, deployment ID, or engine options.
evidence_units.source: git show ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7:aider/main.py, Advanced Model Settings and Coder.create call

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, send_with_retries did not add deployment_id or engine to the keyword arguments passed to openai.ChatCompletion.create.
The changed CLI defines optional arguments for provider API base, API type, API version, deployment ID, and engine.

After parsing and API-key validation, startup assigns openai.api_key and maps each non-null optional provider argument to the corresponding openai.api_* module attribute, reporting each optional assignment through tool output.
Coder.create no longer accepts or assigns provider credentials or endpoint configuration, making the coder factory independent of those startup concerns.
Request construction conditionally copies openai.api_deployment_id to deployment_id and openai.api_engine to engine before hashing the request kwargs and calling openai.ChatCompletion.create.
Relative to the first parent, the merge changes aider/coders/base_coder.py, aider/main.py, docs/faq.md, and four existing test modules, totaling 95 insertions and 46 deletions.
The production Coder.create call in main was reconciled with the new factory interface by removing the API-key and API-base positional arguments.

Existing Coder.create invocations across test_coder, test_commands, test_editblock, and test_wholefile were updated to omit the removed openai_api_key argument, providing static evidence that affected callers were migrated to the new interface.
evidence_units.source: git diff ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758 -- tests/test_coder.py tests/test_commands.py tests/test_editblock.py tests/test_wholefile.py

evidence_units.claim: test_main exercises argument parsing and mocks Coder.create, but the pinned version contains no assertions for the newly added API type, version, deployment ID, engine, or request forwarding behavior.
evidence_units.source: git show 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758:tests/test_main.py; git grep at pinned ref for provider-field names under tests

candidate_atomics.name: centralize-provider-sdk-configuration
candidate_atomics.description: Accept endpoint-specific provider settings at the application boundary and apply only supplied values to the shared provider client before constructing downstream consumers.

semantic_action.intent: Allow one client integration to target provider-compatible endpoints that require additional SDK configuration without embedding startup configuration inside the request consumer.
semantic_action.module_role: application configuration boundary and provider client initializer
semantic_action.pre_state: The application boundary supplies only a key and base, while a downstream consumer factory owns provider SDK mutation and cannot represent type, version, deployment, or engine settings.
semantic_action.post_state: Startup owns provider SDK initialization, exposes the supported endpoint settings, and mutates optional SDK attributes only when corresponding values were supplied.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect parsed option definitions and the pre-construction mapping to provider SDK attributes; verify the downstream factory no longer accepts or assigns provider configuration. Runtime validation remains unavailable in the inspected environment.

candidate_atomics.name: forward-optional-provider-routing-fields
candidate_atomics.description: Conditionally translate configured deployment and engine identifiers into per-request arguments at the provider invocation boundary.

semantic_action.intent: Route requests through endpoints whose invocation contract requires a deployment identifier or engine identifier.
semantic_action.pre_state: Provider requests include generic chat fields but omit endpoint-specific deployment and engine routing fields.
semantic_action.post_state: Each configured routing identifier is included under the provider call's expected request keyword, while absent identifiers add no keyword.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the kwargs assembled immediately before request hashing and ChatCompletion.create; a dedicated behavioral test proving present and absent branches is not in the pinned change.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-consumer-construction-interface
candidate_atomics.description: Remove provider credentials from the consumer factory contract and migrate production and test callers to the configuration-independent constructor.

semantic_action.intent: Keep provider initialization at the application boundary while preserving construction of the request consumer across all known callers.
semantic_action.module_role: consumer factory interface and its call sites
semantic_action.pre_state: The consumer factory requires provider configuration arguments, and production and tests pass those arguments at every construction site.
semantic_action.post_state: The consumer factory accepts only its functional construction inputs, and known production and test callers use the reduced interface.
semantic_action.validation: Diff all known Coder.create call sites and existing constructor-oriented tests to confirm removal of the obsolete argument; the suite could not be executed locally because dependencies were missing.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-a-client-to-provider-specific-endpoint-contracts
candidate_workflows.description: Extend a provider-compatible client by centralizing endpoint configuration, reconciling consumer construction, and translating optional routing values only at the invocation boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Permit the same application to invoke a compatible provider endpoint whose SDK and request contracts require optional endpoint metadata, without forcing provider configuration through the consumer factory.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The client supports a generic key/base configuration, configuration mutation occurs inside a downstream factory, and provider-specific routing values cannot reach the request call.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Application startup initializes all supplied provider settings, the consumer factory is configuration-independent, known callers use its revised interface, and configured request-routing identifiers are forwarded conditionally.
unresolved_or_deferred: No pinned test directly asserts SDK attribute assignment for the new optional configuration values.
No pinned test directly asserts conditional deployment_id or engine forwarding into ChatCompletion.create.
Runtime regression validation is deferred because required Python dependencies are unavailable in the inspection environment.
Behavior when the same process invokes main repeatedly with different optional settings is not established; omitted settings are left untouched on the shared SDK module.
Cross-project pattern promotion is deferred because this episode supplies only one repository workflow and no holdout result.

unresolved_questions: Did PR status checks or an external integration test validate a real alternate endpoint? The evidence bundle does not include checks or review metadata.
Should absent optional settings clear pre-existing SDK module attributes during repeated in-process startup, or intentionally preserve them? The implementation only assigns non-null values.
Are deployment_id and engine mutually exclusive, provider-version-dependent, or both valid together? The pinned code forwards both when both attributes exist.
The attempted local test run was blocked by missing dependencies, so only code, diff, call-site, and test-structure evidence supports this extraction.
